subject: POC trial planning - workload intake (AcmeHealth)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial planning - workload intake (AcmeHealth)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. As discussed, next step is a short POC/trial so you can validate latency, cost, and quality on a representative slice of AcmeHealth traffic. To get the trial scoped and scheduled I need a quick workload intake from you (see bullets below). If you can reply with the numbers / attachments by EOD Thursday we can lock a start date for the week of July 12.

Workload & traffic profile (please include examples where available):
- Typical RPS (average sustained requests per second) and daily peak RPS (brief spikes)
- Concurrency: how many simultaneous client sessions/requests we should support
- Typical prompt length (tokens) and typical model response length (tokens)
- Burst patterns: frequency and duration of spikes (e.g., 60s bursts, hourly spikes at 9am)
- Any multi-region routing or data residency constraints

POC success criteria (draft) — please confirm or edit:
- 95th percentile end-to-end latency under 250ms for interactive endpoints
- No more than 1% error rate on inference calls over a 72-hour run
- Cost estimate within the not-to-exceed threshold we discussed (you mentioned cap of ~$1.50 per 1k generated tokens)
- Model output quality passes 2/3 of sampled eval prompts from your team

Evaluation plan & ownership (proposal):
- Redwood: supply sandbox endpoint(s), pre-configured model variant, and monitoring dashboard
- AcmeHealth (owner: Alex): provide sample traffic and accept test credentials; own quality evals
- Redwood SE (owner: Dylan): set up traffic generator, perf tests, and KV/prefix cache config
- Redwood CS (owner: Marissa): coordinate schedule, success gating, and post-trial readout

Attachments: Redwood POC checklist attached — redwood_poc_checklist.pdf (stub).

Proposed next steps:
1) You send workload numbers + any sample prompts (acme_workload_profile.csv is fine)
2) We align on a 2-week trial window and exact success gates
3) Kickoff call with Dylan & Marissa to confirm test harness and credentials

Would you be available for a 30-min kickoff the week of July 12? I can circulate a calendar invite once we have the intake.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial planning - workload intake (AcmeHealth)

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear checklist. Below are the numbers from our ops team; I attached a small CSV (acme_workload_profile.csv) with sample request/response pairs and timestamps.

Workload summary:
- Typical sustained RPS: ~2 req/s (light traffic overnight)
- Typical daily peak: 12 req/s (short bursts lasting 1-3 minutes during morning syncs)
- Concurrency: up to 8 simultaneous sessions (internal tools + customer-facing widgets)
- Prompt lengths: median ~120 tokens, 90th percentile ~220 tokens
- Model response lengths: median ~180 tokens, 90th percentile ~350 tokens
- Burst patterns: we see micro-bursts up to ~60 req/s for 30–90s when batch jobs run and several hourly spikes at 9am/2pm local time

Success criteria feedback:
- 95p latency <250ms is reasonable for our interactive endpoints (we'll confirm on sample set)
- Error rate under 1% is fine
- Cost cap: aiming for < $1.50 / 1k generated tokens — happy to iterate if needed

Timeline: target pilot start is July 12; prefer a 2-week run with a readout the week of July 26.

I've looped in Priya (ops) on the CC. Please loop in your SE so we can align on test harness and any redaction we need to do for PHI-like fields.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Integrations
AcmeHealth

Attachment: acme_workload_profile.csv (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial planning - workload intake (AcmeHealth)

Alex —

Perfect, this is exactly what we needed. Quick summary / commitments from our side and owners so everyone is aligned:

Confirmed intake details (from your note):
- Sustained RPS: 2 req/s; daily peaks ~12 req/s; micro-bursts up to 60 req/s for 30–90s
- Concurrency target: 8 concurrent sessions
- Prompt/response tokens: median prompt 120 / median response 180; 90p up to 350 tokens
- Timeline: kickoff week of July 12, 2-week trial, readout week of July 26

Redwood owner commitments / next steps:
- Dylan (SE): will build the traffic generator and run an initial smoke/perf test in our sandbox; expected setup time 3 business days after we get sanitized samples
- Marissa (CS): will coordinate schedule and capture success gating; will share a trial schedule draft (trial_schedule_draft.xlsx) by EOD tomorrow
- Ben (me): will own commercial gating and any contract paperwork if we need a temporary trial agreement

Evaluation plan (short):
1) Week 0 (pre-trial): run smoke tests with 10–20% of peak load to verify configs and logging
2) Week 1: ramp to sustained target and run 72-hour stability test; collect latency/error/cost metrics and sample outputs for quality evaluation
3) Week 2: run peak/burst tests and final quality pass; produce readout deck with recommendations

Success criteria (finalize during kickoff):
- 95p latency < 250ms for interactive endpoints under sustained load
- Error rate <1% over the 72-hour run
- Sample quality: AcmeHealth approves >=66% of sampled outputs (sampling plan will be in kickoff)

Security/PHI note: we will work with Priya to confirm redaction or tokenization of PHI-like values before ingesting samples into our test harness. Please flag any fields you want us to obfuscate.

I will schedule the kickoff for Tue July 13 10am PT (tentative) — Dylan and Marissa, does that work for you?

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
